Background: Presently, the majority of photovoltaic grade Si is produced from wafers sliced from boules grown using the Czochralski (Cz) method, which is fed by polycrystalline Si created from the Siemens process. Figure 1 shows the process flow from quartz (SiO ) to finished Si cells with an emphasis on the poly-Si 2 production as feedstock to Cz boule growth [1]. In large poly-Si plants, e.g., those operated by team member Hemlock Semiconductor, metallurgical grade Si, formed from the reduction of quartz in an arc furnace, is then used to produce silicon chlorides via reaction with anhydrous HCl. The mixture is distilled to extract semiconductor grade trichlorosilane (TCS), and represents highest quality Si, in terms of metallic impurity concentration, found throughout the process [2]. To produce poly-Si, TCS is mixed with H in a large chamber and allowed to deposit 2 onto large, electrically-heated seed rods [3]. This step is known as the Siemens process (shown in Fig. 1) and represents nearly one-half the cost of poly-Si, two- thirds of the energy and carbon output from electrical generation, and has a 90 hour cycle time, including time for deposition and then comminution of the poly-Si rods [4]. Adding these poly-Si costs to the Cz boule growth costs contributes to the wafer being one-half the cost of the final PV cell [4]. Fig. 1: The incumbent process for PV silicon production vs. the proposed chemical vapor deposition – float zone reactor. The new process replaces both the Siemens process to generate poly Si feed as well as Czochralski crystallization instead feeding the trichlorosilane gas directly into a semi-continuous float zone puller. This project sought to lower the cost and energy intensity of silicon photovoltaics (PV) manufacturing by modeling a concept for an innovative boule growth process that circumvents the energy-costly Siemens process in polycrystalline (poly)-Si production plants. The right side of Figure 1 shows an illustration the proposed “CVD-Fz” reactor process. This design builds on the traditional Fz process, whereby a poly-Si feed rod produced by the Siemens process is slowly pulled through an RF heater coil causing it to melt and recrystallize as a single crystalline boule. In the envisioned CVD-Fz process, TCS that normally would go to the Siemens process is fed directly into the CVD-Fz reactor, where it deposits as fresh Si onto the poly-Si feed rod in situ, as it is Page 4 of 30 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. being pulled through the RF melting zone. Fz Si wafers are higher purity with high bulk lifetimes (t >20 ms) to enable higher efficiency cells (>26%) with fewer known bulk degradation mechanisms than Czochralski (Cz)-grown wafers. These benefits could reduce the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) of PV by reducing cell cost, increasing cell efficiency, and reducing cell degradation rate, however, Fz wafers are presently more expensive to make vs. the Cz method.
